clue.text: Get-up of some of James II's adherents

definitions.text: Get-up of some of James II's adherents

parts.words: Get-up of some of James II's adherents
parts.note: a 'get-up' is read not as an outfit but as an uprising, the 1715 or 1745 revolt by supporters of the exiled Stuart line

explanation.surface: A costume worn by some followers of the deposed King James.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get-up' suggests clothing; here it means getting up in rebellion. The followers of James II and his heirs were called Jacobites, from Jacobus, Latin for James.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolt is literally a rising up, and the supporters of the Stuart king James were the ones who revolted.

clue.text: Cleaner one to back in a race

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a British cleaning lady
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: to back is to go in reverse, so the little word to is read from right to left

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady puts a bet on one runner in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is British slang for a cleaning woman. The definition is loose: the answer is a vehicle used in a race, not the race itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle of antiquity was raced in Roman circuses.

clue.text: Scottish isle, albeit oriental

parts.note: albeit means even though, which is but in its sense of yet
oriental means eastern, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: A Scottish island described as having an eastern feel.
explanation.definitionFit: This island sits in the Firth of Clyde off western Scotland.

clue.text: Householder who is slow to move

definitions.text: Householder who is slow to move

parts.words: Householder who is slow to move
parts.note: a creature that carries its home on its back and plods, read as a sluggish homeowner reluctant to relocate

explanation.surface: A homeowner who takes ages to get round to moving house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Householder' suggests a person; it is an animal whose shell is its house, and 'slow to move' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: This reptile carries its shell like a house and is famously sluggish.

clue.text: Carped about getting the bird

indicators.note: about signals moving the letters around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone complained once they had been booed off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting the bird' suggests being jeered; 'the bird' alone is the definition, with 'getting' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcap is an old country name for the goldfinch, with its red face.

clue.text: "Hang," he said, being forced to serve

indicators.note: being here signals the letters becoming something else, a rearrangement of the quoted words

explanation.surface: A protesting sailor curses as he is press-ganged aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of HANG and HE SAID rearrange; the indicator 'being' is weak, but the surface makes the clue nearly an &lit, since the victim swears as he is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors were once drugged or tricked into crewing ships bound for the Chinese port, so the word means coerced into service.

clue.text: One neat newly-born

indicators.note: newly-born suggests the letters are freshly made into a new form, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A tidy little baby, just arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: ONE and NEAT rearrange, and the whole clue describes the result: a newly born infant.
explanation.definitionFit: A neonate is a baby in its first weeks of life, a tidy newly arrived infant.

clue.text: Recording instrument to mesmerise in a way

indicators.note: in a way suggests putting the letters into a different way or order

explanation.surface: A device for recording, used to hypnotise people somehow.
explanation.definitionFit: This device records the tremors of earthquakes.

clue.text: Given a pasting

parts.note: pasting is read both as a heavy beating and as being coated in a paste of flour and egg before frying

explanation.surface: Someone who has been well and truly thrashed.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'pasting' is British slang for a thrashing; batter is also the paste fish is fried in.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaten hard, and also coated in flour paste for frying, as fish in a British chip shop.

clue.text: Humble dwelling where there's trouble to be found

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble, as in much ado
to be found means to exist, which is to be

explanation.surface: A modest cottage that turns out to be a source of strife.
explanation.definitionFit: A sun-dried mud-brick house is a simple home in the American Southwest.

clue.text: Timid extras needed for filling in another job

indicators.note: needed suggests the letters being kneaded, worked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Shy film extras wanted to stand in on a different job.
explanation.walkthrough: TIMID and EXTRAS rearrange. The definition is cryptic: this job is stuffing, or filling in, another creature's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffer of dead animals literally fills in another creature's skin for a living.

clue.text: Covetous of a sixpence once

parts.note: sixpence in old British money was written 6d, which is Roman VI plus d for the old penny

explanation.surface: Greedy for an old small coin.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 British money counted pence with d, so sixpence was VI D in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager and greedy for something, the old phrase being avid of.

clue.text: Sing a carol, for a change, with this instrument

indicators.note: for a change says the letters are altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An invitation to vary things by singing carols with a woodwind accompaniment.
explanation.definitionFit: The English horn is an alto woodwind in the oboe family.

clue.text: Important, dash it, most important

annotationWithheld.why: Important, dash it, most important (3-7): EMINENT gives important and the definition is most important, but nothing in 'dash it' gives PRE; the clue as held looks garbled and no search found the original.

clue.text: Hobby which can increase one's income?

definitions.meaning: a pastime one pursues for pleasure
money paid by a bank on savings, adding to earnings

explanation.surface: A pastime that might also be a nice little earner.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a leisure pursuit and the return paid on capital lent or saved.

clue.text: Managed, with difficulty, a successful party

parts.note: a made man is one who has succeeded
a do is British slang for a party

explanation.surface: Someone just about got by, and had a good party.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'do' is everyday British for a party or celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: To get by with what is available, coping despite lacking things.

clue.text: Lent 3 something to chew over

indicators.note: over suggests turning things over, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: 3 refers to the answer to 3 down, the Scottish island

explanation.surface: A forty-day fast gives you something to think about.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' points to the answer to 3-down, BUTE; LENT plus BUTE rearrange. 'chew over' looks like the phrase for thinking, but 'over' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The areca seed wrapped in leaves is chewed as a mild stimulant across South Asia.

clue.text: Dodges the Spanish dues anyway

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the

indicators.note: anyway suggests the letters set down in any order at all

explanation.surface: A Spaniard avoids paying fees one way or another.
explanation.definitionFit: Avoids or escapes, as someone slipping away from a pursuer.

clue.text: Relative to an indecorous state

definitions.note: the noun phrase stands loosely for the adjective describing that state

parts.note: an uncle is a family relation

explanation.surface: A family member reduced to a rather improper condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Impure or defiled, in the moral or ritual sense of being improper.

clue.text: Evening piece still played outside nowadays

indicators.note: outside means the word for calm wraps around the other piece

parts.note: still means calm, peaceful
AD, anno Domini, labels the present era

explanation.surface: A piece of evening music still performed outdoors today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still played outside' suggests open-air music, but 'outside' is the container signal and 'played' only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A song sung at evening beneath a lover's window, from Italian sera, evening.

clue.text: No gentleman, Ian concludes, from Nova Scotia

indicators.note: concludes means the name comes at the end, after the other piece

parts.note: a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably, so no gentleman is a cad

explanation.surface: Ian decides that someone from Nova Scotia is no gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Acadia was the old French colony covering Nova Scotia, so its people were Acadians.

clue.text: A grand garb used for jumble

indicators.note: used suggests second-hand clothing remade, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: An outfit of fine clothes donated to a jumble sale.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumble sale is a British charity sale of second-hand goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscellaneous collection of odds and ends, like a jumbled bag of scraps.

clue.text: Schemes of friends around the country

indicators.note: around means the word for friends surrounds the country

parts.note: mates is British for friends
China is the country in question

explanation.surface: Plans made by pals from across the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Plots or contrives, especially with crafty intent.

clue.text: Hollow warning

definitions.meaning: a hole in a hillside or under a cliff
Latin for beware, the schoolboy cry when a teacher approaches

explanation.surface: An empty warning, a threat with nothing behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: British public-school slang used the Latin word for beware as a lookout's cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun for a natural hollow in rock, and old school slang for look out.

clue.text: Long way round the Algarve capital

parts.note: far means a long way off
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: It is a long trip round to reach the main city of the Algarve.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the regional seat of Portugal's southern Algarve coast.

clue.text: Leading lady is returning in the Jumblies' unseaworthy craft

indicators.note: returning means these pieces are read back the other way

parts.note: Eve, the first woman, is the original leading lady

explanation.surface: A star actress comes back aboard a leaky boat from a nonsense poem.
explanation.walkthrough: In Edward Lear's poem The Jumblies, the Jumblies went to sea in a perforated kitchen utensil.
explanation.definitionFit: In Lear's nonsense verse the Jumblies sailed in a mesh strainer, a craft full of holes.

clue.text: Favourite son with a preserve in West African region

indicators.note: in means the preserve is placed inside the region

parts.note: Benin is the West African country, once also a kingdom
jam is a fruit preserve

explanation.surface: A beloved boy turns up with a pot of jam in West Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Jacob's youngest child was his most cherished, so the name means a favourite youngest child.

clue.text: Where drunks may find themselves uncomfortably placed

definitions.text: Where drunks may find themselves uncomfortably placed

parts.words: Where drunks may find themselves uncomfortably placed
parts.note: tight is read as drunk, so a drunk slumped in the angle of a room is literally in a difficult spot

explanation.surface: Inebriated people ending up awkwardly stuck somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' is British slang for drunk, so the idiom for a difficult situation is read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in a difficult spot, and tight is slang for drunk.
